scope: Second targeted screen, maximum seven additional candidates. Existing graph/site/main review files remain unchanged. These are research proposals, not accepted graph additions or influence claims.

count_definitions.raw_strict: Exact release work key citing dissertations among 7,107 strict in-analysis records, including undated records. Not raw citation occurrences.
count_definitions.dated: Public export exact work key citing dissertations among 6,794 records with nonempty year.
count_definitions.series: Eight public periods by four regions; programme/repository geography, not geography studied.
count_definitions.limits: Different work and translation counts are not summed. Citation presence does not establish rhetorical use, influence or agreement. Corpus years may identify editions. First-author work keys do not imply sole authorship.

candidates.content_classification: Explicit conceptual/method intervention through travel-writing criticism.
candidates.current_identity_status: No indexed person record or standalone entry for this exact person in revision 1.164.

current_coverage.detail: Imperial knowledge, representation and hybridity already have strands; Pratt and Imperial Eyes are absent.
Connected histories and encounters are present but do not supply the specific contact-zone/anti-conquest analytical vocabulary.

candidates.content_gap: Travel writing as an unequal encounter and the relationship between scientific description, imperial vision and transculturation have no named Pratt treatment.
candidates.proposed_action: Research Pratt as a contributor in post, with a bounded travel-writing/contact-zone strand; compare with Said and existing colonial-representation approaches without treating them as synonymous.
limits: 143 dated versus 145 raw strict dissertations for the exact work key; do not call this a first-author total.
First-edition 1992 and expanded second-edition 2008 content must be separated.
Publisher contents establish the intervention’s scope, not its detailed arguments or reception.
Many citations might use a specific colonial case rather than the concepts; rhetorical use requires passages.

candidates.content_classification: Historically specific synthetic intervention into nation formation; framework use must be established rather than assumed.
candidates.current_identity_status: No indexed person record or standalone entry for this exact person in revision 1.164.

current_coverage.detail: Anderson and invented traditions, plus gender/nation, are already covered; Colley is absent.
British political culture is present; the latter strand mainly stages language/class debates, not the Britons interpretation.

candidates.content_gap: A major empirical test of national-identity construction through Protestantism, war, empire and internal differences is missing; adding another generic nationalism field would miss the actual gap.
candidates.proposed_action: Add a researched British national-identity case/strand, including the question of how far Britishness was shared and whose exclusions supported it. Captives can widen the imperial frame after separate reading.
limits: Britons 121 dated/123 raw; Captives 34/34. They are not editions of the same work.
Citation frequency does not show acceptance of the Protestant/war narrative or establish a universal model.
The current publisher listing is a revised 2009 edition; institutional bibliography verifies the 1992 original.

candidates.content_classification: Conceptual historiographical intervention through historical studies of representation, expectation and Indigenous modernity.
candidates.current_identity_status: No indexed person record or standalone entry for this exact person in revision 1.164.

current_coverage.detail: Existing Vine Deloria Jr. is a different person and must retain identity and works.
Research authority and Vine Deloria’s institutional critique already exist; they do not cover Philip Deloria’s two books.
National identity exists as a field question but lacks this appropriation/Indianness argument.
Substantial field coverage exists; no need to imply an absence of settler-colonial analysis.

candidates.content_gap: The relation between non-Native identity-making and Native people’s participation in modernity is absent as a named two-sided research problem.
candidates.proposed_action: Research a Philip J. Deloria identity and distinct representation/expectation strands across indigenous, culture and nationalismstudies. Preserve Native agency and separate white appropriation from Indigenous historical experience.
limits: Playing Indian 79 dated/79 raw; Unexpected Places 65/65. Do not sum to an author total.
Philip J. and Vine Jr. are distinct identities; a surname-level match is especially dangerous here.
The books use different objects and questions; no single influence edge follows from their common authorship.

candidates.content_classification: Explicit conceptual/method intervention in colonial power, expertise and political economy through Egyptian cases.
candidates.current_identity_status: No indexed person record or standalone entry for this exact person in revision 1.164.

current_coverage.detail: Colonial knowledge and representation are covered; Mitchell is absent.
Expertise and knowledge politics exist but do not supply Mitchell’s techno-politics.
Classification/profession histories exist; no named Mitchell argument.
Capitalism debates are present, but not his question about the practical production of a national economy.

candidates.content_gap: The production of colonial order and the constitution of expertise/economy through mixed technical, social and political practices lack a named intervention.
candidates.proposed_action: Research Mitchell as a cross-field contributor and attach bounded strands to post/STS/political economy. The 1991 preface supplies direct evidence for a specific Foucault engagement and qualification; do not generalize this into a full genealogy.
limits: Rule of Experts 65 dated/66 raw; Colonising Egypt 41/41.
Different Mitchell identities exist in the corpus and graph: Timothy is not Juliet Mitchell, Mitchell Dean, Michele Mitchell or W.J.T. Mitchell.
Egyptian case studies need attention to their historical evidence and Arabic/European sources; not every citation is a general framework use.
1988 original and June 1991 paperback preface must be distinguished.

candidates.content_classification: Political-theoretical and historical interpretation; not simply subject-area scholarship and not automatically a school of historians.
candidates.current_identity_status: No indexed person record or standalone entry for this exact person in revision 1.164.

current_coverage.detail: Administrative destruction, perpetrator interpretation and representation already exist; Arendt is not indexed or substantively named.
Explanation and historical knowledge are already debated, without Arendt’s retrospective origins/elements distinction.
The source title The Human Condition in the Anthropocene is Chakrabarty’s own 2015 lecture. Its lexical overlap does not establish coverage of Arendt’s book.
On violence appears as an ordinary phrase/section label; without named Arendt attribution it is not evidence for her 1970 book.

candidates.content_gap: No named treatment of totalitarianism as a historically novel form, origins versus causes, or the labour/work/action distinctions, despite substantial cited presence.
candidates.proposed_action: Research an Arendt contributor identity and bounded conceptual treatment, likely across political theory, Holocaust interpretation and historical explanation. Treat controversies over totalitarianism and Eichmann as research tasks before drawing critique edges.
limits: Origins 72 dated/72 raw; Human Condition 36/36; Eichmann 30/30; On Violence 28/28.
Corpus years 1973, 1998 and 2006 are cited editions; originals 1951, 1958 and 1963 need separate sourced chronology.
Arendt’s writings can be both objects of intellectual history and conceptual resources; counts cannot separate those roles.
Do not infer that later historians agree with her interpretations, that one model explains all regimes, or that a general phrase is a book citation.

candidates.content_classification: Historiographical programme across political symbolism, national mobilization, normative bodies and commemoration; individual works also serve specific regional subjects.
candidates.current_identity_status: No indexed person record or standalone entry for this exact person in revision 1.164.

current_coverage.detail: National symbolism and gender are present but no Mosse identity or named works.
Masculinity already has a strand; missing Mosse is an underdeveloped connection rather than absent masculinity history.
Winter, Young and memory/monument work are covered; Mosse’s Fallen Soldiers is absent.
Political symbolism is covered through other contributors; add this particular programme and its limits.

candidates.content_gap: A named body of work links national political liturgy to masculinity, sexuality and war commemoration, without being equivalent to the existing nationalist-theory roster.
candidates.proposed_action: Research Mosse as a contributor across existing fields, with several qualified work-based contexts. Use specific reception or reply passages to distinguish an intellectual programme from the claim of one general theory.
limits: Fallen Soldiers 44 dated/45 raw; Image of Man 32/33; Nationalism and Sexuality 27/27; Crisis 22/23; Nationalization 22/23. These cannot be summed to an author total.
1975 original Nationalization and 2023 critical edition are separate chronology events.
German/European historical focus is substantial; do not infer a global universalization from a national-culture case.
Existing group fields already cover all of these topics, so the task is a named explanatory bridge rather than five new fields.

candidates.content_classification: Specific historiographical/method intervention: historicizing perception and sensory social distinctions, using historical subjects rather than assuming timeless senses.
candidates.current_identity_status: No indexed person record or standalone entry for this exact person in revision 1.164.

current_coverage.detail: Febvre 1941 and earlier sensibilities already appear; Corbin himself identifies that programme as a resource in the primary 1993 interview.
Cultural and visual practices are present, but no explicit sensory-history strand or Corbin identity.
Medical/health history is present. Smell, hygiene and sensory classifications would connect to it without reducing sensory history to medical progress.

candidates.content_gap: Historical change in sensory perception and the social organization of smell remain invisible as an explicit method. This complements the earlier emotions proposal but should not be treated as the same field.
candidates.proposed_action: Research a sensory-history strand using the exact Foul and Fragrant work and Corbin’s methodological self-account. First establish the cited edition and read selected passages before assigning specific causal claims or influence edges.
limits: The exact frozen key has 31 dated/31 raw, with 15 Europe, 12 Canada and 4 US; it is a modest regional signal.
The normalized work key is French while the title and year describe the English 1986 translation. Keep this existing record intact; no automatic French/English union or publication-date repair.
The book’s contents and an interview page were checked, not the full book.
Sensory history is not automatically emotions history; the proposed content should preserve this distinction.
